outcome.candidate_text:
The smallest value is \(\boxed{11}\).

For necessity, let the first player write five copies of \(23\) and four copies of \(24\). Their total is
\[
5\cdot23+4\cdot24=211.
\]
Every proper sublist has sum at most \(211-23=188\), while the whole list has sum \(211\). Thus no sublist sum lies in \([190,210]\), so \(N=10\), and hence every smaller \(N\), is insufficient.

For sufficiency, consider any permitted list. Among all sublists whose sums do not exceed \(211\), choose one with maximum sum \(m\). If \(m\ge189\), its sum already lies in \([189,211]\). Suppose instead that \(m\le188\).

Because the entire list has sum at least \(200>m\), some entry \(b\) is not selected. Maximality gives \(m+b>211\), so
\[
b\ge212-m.
\]
Since \(b\le25\), it follows that \(m\ge187\). Hence \(m\in\{187,188\}\).

If \(m=187\), then every unselected entry equals \(25\). The selected sublist contains an entry \(x\le23\): otherwise, if it had at most seven entries its sum would be at most \(7\cdot25=175\), while if it had at least eight entries its sum would be at least \(8\cdot24=192\). Replacing \(x\) by an unselected \(25\) gives sum
\[
187+25-x=212-x\in[189,211].
\]

Now let \(m=188\). Every unselected entry is \(24\) or \(25\). If some unselected entry is \(24\), the same counting argument shows that the selected sublist contains an entry \(x\le23\); replacing it by \(24\) gives \(212-x\in[189,211]\).

It remains that all unselected entries equal \(25\). We claim that the selected sublist contains some sublist of sum \(r\in[2,24]\). If it contains an entry between \(2\) and \(24\), take that entry. Otherwise all its entries are \(1\) or \(25\). Since \(188\not\equiv0,1\pmod{25}\), there must be at least two entries equal to \(1\); take those two, giving \(r=2\). Adding an unselected \(25\) and removing this sublist gives sum
\[
188+25-r=213-r\in[189,211].
\]

Thus every permitted list has a sublist sum in
\[
[189,211]=[200-11,200+11].
\]
Therefore \(N=11\) is sufficient and minimal.
outcome.stop_reason: The lower-bound list excludes every \(N\le10\). The maximal-sublist argument repairs the previously incomplete \(s=213\) case by showing that when the added entry is \(25\), selected entries of total between \(2\) and \(24\) can always be removed.
